facts.text: On this date in 1889, Brazil abolished its monarchy overnight — Emperor Pedro II was asleep when generals staged the coup, and he learned he'd been deposed only at breakfast.
On this date in 1920, the League of Nations held its first assembly in Geneva, representing 41 nations — yet the country that proposed it, the United States, never joined.
More people live inside a 40-mile radius of Jakarta than in the entire country of Australia.
The city of Chongqing, China, has more people than Canada. It is a single municipality — not a province — covering an area roughly the size of Austria.
Mongolia is the world's least densely populated sovereign nation, with about 2 people per square kilometer, yet its capital Ulaanbaatar holds nearly half the entire national population.
On this day in 1867, the Chicago Produce Exchange opened — the ancestor of today's CME Group, which now clears over $1 quadrillion in contracts annually.
On November 15, 1999, the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act repealed Glass-Steagall, letting commercial and investment banks merge again after 66 years apart. Nine years later, the financial system collapsed.
The entire market cap of the New York Stock Exchange in 1900 was roughly $4 billion — less than a single hour of Apple's current revenue run rate.
Saudi Aramco briefly hit a $2 trillion valuation in 2019, making it worth more than the GDP of Italy. It got there after one day of public trading.

The Dutch tulip mania of 1637 is remembered as irrational hysteria, but the crash was partly triggered by a legal change that let buyers cancel futures contracts for a small fee — a rational exit, badly timed.

On this date in 1930, humans first confirmed the stratosphere contains ozone. That thin molecular layer, just 3mm thick if compressed to sea level pressure, is the only reason complex life exists on land.
Your bones are not static scaffolding. The entire human skeleton replaces itself roughly every 10 years through a continuous process of osteoclasts dissolving old bone while osteoblasts rebuild it.
On this date in 1738, Daniel Bernoulli published Hydrodynamica, establishing that faster-moving fluids exert less pressure — the principle that lets 500-ton aircraft leave the ground.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its matter would weigh roughly 10 million tons on Earth.

Trees in a forest actively share sugar through fungal networks connecting their roots. A dying tree will receive carbon from neighbors, suggesting the network redistributes resources rather than simply leaking them.
On this day in 1777, the Continental Congress adopted the Articles of Confederation — America's first constitution, which lasted just 8 years before being quietly abandoned as unworkable.
Oxford University was teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. Oxford dates to 1096; Tenochtitlan wasn't founded until 1325.

On this day in 1864, Sherman began his March to the Sea — 60,000 troops cutting a 300-mile swath through Georgia in a deliberate experiment in breaking civilian morale, the template for modern total war.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She died in 30 BC; the pyramid was finished around 2560 BC.
The fax machine was invented in 1843 — before the American Civil War, before the telephone, before Edison was born. Japan's attachment to fax technology isn't nostalgia; it's just very long loyalty.

Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012. It spread until the feeling finally had a name.

Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh longing for a home that may never have existed — nostalgia, grief, and belonging fused into one untranslatable ache. English requires a full sentence to say what Welsh says in three syllables.

On this day in 1532, Pizarro captured the Inca emperor Atahualpa at Cajamarca. The Quechua word 'llaqta,' meaning city or homeland, survives in place names across the Andes — a language outlasting the empire that spoke it.

On this day in 1969, the Moratorium March drew 500,000 to Washington. The Latin root of 'moratorium' is 'morari' — to delay — making it literally a pause, not an end. The word has always been careful about what it promises.

Mamihlapinatapai (n.): a Yaghan word from Tierra del Fuego for a look shared between two people who both want something neither will initiate. The Yaghan language has fewer than ten remaining speakers. The feeling is universal.

On this date in 2021, Bitcoin reached $65,000 for the first time — then lost half its value within weeks. The peak lasted under 24 hours before selling pressure from newly listed Coinbase options overwhelmed spot demand.

On Nov 15, 2018, Bitcoin Cash split into two chains mid-block 556,766. The hash war between Craig Wright and Roger Ver burned an estimated $10M in miner revenue in a single week settling a whitepaper dispute.

Ethereum's gas limit is set by miners, not the protocol. Blocks can hold more or fewer transactions based on miner votes — a design choice that has quietly tripled throughput without a single hard fork.
Satoshi's known wallet addresses — roughly 1.1 million BTC mined in 2009 — have never moved a single satoshi. On-chain analysts can identify them by the Patoshi pattern in early nonce sequences.
The DAO hack in 2016 didn't steal ETH — it locked 3.6 million ETH in a recursive withdrawal loop the attacker couldn't fully exit. Ethereum's hard fork happened before they could drain it cleanly.

On this date in 2022, Meta released Galactica — a 120B-parameter model trained on scientific literature. It was pulled 72 hours later after researchers demonstrated it generated fluent, confident nonsense about bears and the history of time.
On this date in 2017, Google Brain published 'Attention Is All You Need,' introducing the transformer. Every major language model in production today descends directly from that eight-author paper.

AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins — essentially the entire UniProt database — using less compute time than a single experimental X-ray crystallography lab produces in a year.

GPT-4's training run is estimated to have cost around $100 million. The original GPT, trained in 2018, cost roughly $43,000. That is a 2,000x cost increase in six years, tracking a capability jump that no other engineering field has matched at this pace.

RLHF — the technique that made ChatGPT feel coherent — was originally developed to teach robots to backflip. The 2017 OpenAI paper used human preference signals to train simulated locomotion, not language.
